newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crudes firm late after heating oil spurt.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crudes firm late after heating oil spurt.

text.p: U.S. domestic crudes chalked up solid gains late Friday pulled higher by short covering and heating oil gains, traders said.
A stalled Iraq oil-for-food deal also gave the market more upward momentum, as funds were seen unwilling to compromise long positions despite the overheated environment.
"Every time people have gone short, they have lost money. We could very well see higher levels next week," a Houston trader said, citing near-term resistance at $23.95 a barrel.
October West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was at $23.80-90 a barrel, up 60 cents from Thursday.
Domestic grade differentials were largely mixed with light crudes slightly stronger, and heavy crudes turning softer.
But traders said this was due more to intraday demand than a longer-term trend.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St James traded between WTI plus 35-37 cents, moderately above Thursday's plus 35 cents.
West Texas Intermediate Posting Plus traded at postings plus $2.34 a barrel, but firmer over the session with the revival of the Oct/Nov spread to 68 cents, up five cents.
Heavy, sour grades were mixed with West Texas Sour/Midland holding at Thursday's higher levels, at WTI minus $1.18.
But Eugene Island drifted three cents lower to minus $1.08/1.05.
Competing heavy Latin American cargoes of Oriente, Canadon Seco and Mendanitos were seen available to the U.S., although buyers were seen marking time and not showing bids.
Offers for Oriente were pegged around WTI minus $1.80 cif.
